assumptions: All four first-semester intake cohorts are retained; no graduation, withdrawal or repeat rates were supplied.
Intake values come from the current individual-major scenario rows; CS/AI/CYBER retain equal estimated shares derived from their original combined intake.
Unknown second-semester intakes are excluded, not treated as confirmed zero.
Normal progression: 2026/2025/2024/2023 cohorts attend study semesters 1/3/5/7 in first semester 2026.
An inferred eight-semester, 132-credit plan respects strict prerequisites, permitted concurrency, elective limits and 90-credit thresholds.
Credit loads are balanced without using current offerings to choose semester parity; the inferred plan is not an official recommended study plan.
Estimated groups are demand batches; their members can attend different sections, each retaining the complete requested course combination.
Only currently offered exact course codes are assigned; unavailable planned courses are explicitly reported.
Enrollment among different reference delivery/equipment pools is proportional to their reference counts; these proportions remain estimates.
Legacy course codes without an exact plan match have unknown demand and are not assigned the old synthetic counts.
The first semester after admission has 12 total credits, including 6 to 9 university requirement credits, for both fall and spring entrants.

Only faculty compulsory, major compulsory and selected major electives are scheduled. University courses remain context for degree progression and completed-credit thresholds, and are excluded from timetable demand.
Each representative student selects exactly 9 major-elective credits over the full degree, not 9 each semester; unselected electives do not create sections.

Every IT course is offered each calendar semester. Coverage profiles may differ by one academic step, representing estimated varied progression. Their own completed-course histories satisfy prerequisites; no course is assigned solely by calendar parity. Shares are illustrative, not measured acceleration or repeat rates.

Prerequisite-valid paths per major: {'AI': 5, 'CIS': 4, 'CS': 4, 'CYBER': 4, 'SE': 5}. Each intake is divided equally using integer remainders. Extra coverage paths ensure every IT course has positive current-semester demand. These are scenario estimates, not observed shares.

Students of the same major/year can have different completed courses, current course bundles and major electives. Every path still completes 132 degree credits and 9 major-elective credits; credits are not reduced to force room feasibility.
